questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Given that $P(A)=\dfrac1{10}$, $P(B)=\dfrac25$ and that $A$ and $B$ are independent. Calculate

(a) $P(A\cap B)$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
For independent events, $P(A\cap B)=P(A)\times P(B)$:

$$P(A\cap B)=\frac1{10}\times\frac25=\frac2{50}=\frac1{25}.$$

**$P(A\cap B)=\dfrac1{25}=0.04$.**

$A'$ (not $A$) and $B$ are also independent, with $P(A')=1-\dfrac1{10}=\dfrac9{10}$:

$$P(A'\cap B)=\frac9{10}\times\frac25=\frac{18}{50}=\frac9{25}.$$

Check: $P(A'\cap B)=P(B)-P(A\cap B)=\dfrac25-\dfrac1{25}=\dfrac9{25}$ ✓.

**$P(A'\cap B)=\dfrac9{25}=0.36$.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(ii) A bag contains 3 red and 3 white balls. Two balls are drawn from the bag, one after the other, without replacement.

(a) Draw a tree diagram to illustrate all the possible outcomes. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
There are $6$ balls in the bag at the first draw, and $5$ at the second (no replacement). Draw two stages of branches, each branch labelled with its probability:

- **First ball:** R with probability $\dfrac36=\dfrac12$; W with probability $\dfrac36=\dfrac12$.
- **Second ball after a red first ball** (2 red and 3 white left): R with probability $\dfrac25$; W with probability $\dfrac35$.
- **Second ball after a white first ball** (3 red and 2 white left): R with probability $\dfrac35$; W with probability $\dfrac25$.

The four outcomes, with their probabilities (multiply along the branches):

| Outcome | Probability |
|---|---|
| RR | $\dfrac12\times\dfrac25=\dfrac15$ |
| RW | $\dfrac12\times\dfrac35=\dfrac3{10}$ |
| WR | $\dfrac12\times\dfrac35=\dfrac3{10}$ |
| WW | $\dfrac12\times\dfrac25=\dfrac15$ |

Check: $\dfrac15+\dfrac3{10}+\dfrac3{10}+\dfrac15=1$ ✓.
themes: tree diagrams and conditional probability (additional maths)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Using the tree diagram, calculate the probability that

(ii)(b) one ball of each colour is drawn. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
One ball of each colour means RW or WR (two branches, added):

$$P=P(RW)+P(WR)=\frac3{10}+\frac3{10}=\frac35.$$

**$P(\text{one of each colour})=\dfrac35=0.6$.**
themes: tree diagrams and conditional probability (additional maths)

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(c) at most one white ball is drawn. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
At most one white ball means $0$ or $1$ white ball: the outcomes RR, RW and WR (everything except WW).

$$P=P(RR)+P(RW)+P(WR)=\frac15+\frac3{10}+\frac3{10}=\frac45.$$

Check: $1-P(WW)=1-\dfrac15=\dfrac45$ ✓.

**$P(\text{at most one white})=\dfrac45=0.8$.**
themes: tree diagrams and conditional probability (additional maths)
